svg.title: rEach and Teach: reaching the instructors
svg.desc: Seven channels between the student's computer and the instructors. Hands, fault reports, feedback notes and live sessions go out to Teach; replies, announcements and course controls come back. Notes, live sessions and the student's own help requests wait for the student's yes.
svg.text: Four ways out to the instructors and three ways back. Notes and live sessions go only on the student's yes.
course server · read and answered by the instructors
The student asks, and rEach raises one by itself at the third failed try. Every hand
has a type: a grade question, a technical issue, an extension request and more.
the instructors see its type and reply
A fault that stops enrollment, sign-in, sync, qualify or submit is reported the
first time, any other the third time in a day; never a prompt or code.
and says when the fix reaches the student
Anything that can wait: an idea, a question, a problem, how the pace feels. Shown
word for word, sent on a yes, named or anonymous.
an anonymous one is stored without a name
On the student's typed yes the instructors' assistant works with rEach. Each action
it asks for, and each message sent, needs another yes.
between rEach and the instructors' assistant
Replies to hands and named notes arrive with the next sync. A problem the course
server is already fixing carries a workaround until the fix arrives.
picked up on the next sync
Shown once, word for word, and kept in a list by date. A moved due time is shown
once, with the earlier and the new time.
to the course, a group or one student
A pause stops course work, a hold stops submitting, a test locks all but the test.
rEach enforces each in code, and reach support keeps working.
